based_in.value: Tel Aviv, Israel (also has US operations)

growth_signal.value: Valuation roughly doubled within about a year across funding rounds, from $3 billion to $4.8 billion to $6.4 billion.

raised.value: $400M Series F (Sept 2026) at a $6.4B valuation; earlier raised $250M Series E at $4.8B and $175M Series D at $3B

entry.idea: So much work now happens inside a web browser, and soon AI agents will click and type there too, but companies have no way to see or control what happens on that screen, so Island built a business browser with company rules and security built in.
entry.lesson: Rebuild an everyday tool around a business's biggest unsolved security problem, and let a new technology wave (AI agents) keep raising the value of that control point.
entry.name: Island

growth.reason: Its valuation more than doubled in about a year across back-to-back mega-rounds, with real dollar numbers each time.

market.reason: Almost every company with office workers, and now AI agents, needs a way to secure what happens in the browser.

tech.reason: It built a full business browser with deep controls and created the category, though large rivals like Chrome are adding similar enterprise features.

entry.twist: It created the 'enterprise browser' category from scratch, and it now also watches and governs AI agents acting inside the browser on people's behalf, catching risky things like copying sensitive data into the wrong place.
entry.who_pays: Large companies and government agencies that want to control what employees, contractors and AI agents can do on company systems.
entry.why_now: More business software runs in the browser than ever, and AI agents are starting to operate there too, so companies need a new place to enforce security and compliance rules.
